1.point: The Munajat's confession of a neglected soul opens the chapter; the soul is what we know everything with, so irfan begins there, and this chapter shows why and how knowing ourselves is the way to knowing God.
steps: A familiar prayer confesses a neglected soul (hook)
The confession implies the soul is a trust that can be neglected
The soul deserves care because all knowing happens through it
Recall: the soul knows itself and its images directly (knowledge by presence)
Knowing God must be this kind of direct knowing, so it happens in the soul; the chapter will show why and how

2.point: A human life is decided by what is done with the soul: purify it and succeed, betray it and fail.
steps: Surah al-Shams builds to an oath by the soul and its God-given discernment
The verses that follow make success and failure turn on purifying or betraying the soul
Therefore the human story is the soul's story, and the Munajat's neglected soul is the failure the surah names

3.point: God and the soul are lost together and found together, so knowing God starts with knowing the soul.
steps: Forgetting God causes forgetting the soul (al-Hashr)
Remembering God turns attention back to the soul
Losing the soul loses faith (al-An'am), because a soul that is seen points to its Maker
Both forgetting and knowing run in both directions; the hadith states it
The saying holds because the soul reflects its Maker (without being part of God)
Therefore knowing God begins with knowing the soul

4.point: God is present to us now and mirrored in the soul; the only obstacle is a veil over the soul, so the seeker's task is to lift it, and to begin in this life.
steps: We are already in God's presence but do not perceive Him
So the journey is veil-lifting by purification, not travel
The veils come off for every soul at the promised meeting
What is seen there is the soul as a reflection of God
How much is seen then depends on how much is seen now
Therefore begin lifting the veils in this life
Conclusion: the way to God runs through knowing and purifying the self

¶1.label: advance
¶1.why: The hook: a prayer most readers know, narrowed to one confessional line.

¶2.label: advance
¶2.why: Turns the confession into the chapter's subject: the soul is a trust that can be neglected.

¶3.label: advance
¶3.why: Supplies why the soul matters: all knowing is done with it. ¶5 depends on this.

¶4.label: advance
¶4.why: Recalls knowledge by presence, which ¶5 needs for 'this same direct knowing'. Longer than the one or two sentences the opening allows, but the step is required.

¶5.label: advance
¶5.why: Draws the conclusion (irfan begins with the soul) and states what the chapter will establish.

¶6.label: advance
¶6.why: Sets up Surah al-Shams: the oath by the soul and its gift of discernment, leading into the verses.

¶7.label: advance
¶7.why: Supplies the step the verses carry: success and failure turn on what is done with the soul.

¶8.label: advance
¶8.why: States the section's conclusion once and ties the Munajat's neglect to the surah's failure.

¶9.label: advance
¶9.why: Links Section 2 to this one and names the cause of losing the soul: forgetting God.

¶10.label: aside
¶10.why: Who counts as having forgotten, and that it need not mean punishment, is a pastoral clarification. No later sentence uses it; the chain runs from ¶9 straight to ¶11.

¶11.label: advance
¶11.why: The first direction of 'known together': remembering God brings attention back to the soul.

¶12.label: advance
¶12.why: Introduces the reverse direction: losing the soul loses faith (al-An'am).

¶13.label: advance
¶13.why: Gives the mechanism the point needs: a soul that is seen points to its Creator, unlike the body.

¶14.label: advance
¶14.why: Joins the two directions and brings in the hadith that states them in one line. The first sentence summarises, but the hadith is a new step.

¶15.label: advance
¶15.why: Explains why the saying holds (the soul reflects its Maker) and closes the pantheism door. Section 4 reuses the reflection idea.

¶16.label: restate
¶16.why: 'Knowing God begins with knowing the soul' was already delivered by the hadith in ¶14 and the reflection argument in ¶15. Tabataba'i is a second authority saying the same thing; nothing later uses him.

¶17.label: advance
¶17.why: God is present now; the soul lacks perception. The premise the whole section rests on.

¶18.label: advance
¶18.why: Draws the consequence: the journey is veil-lifting by purification, not travel. Introduces hijab and qurb.

¶19.label: advance
¶19.why: Veils come off for every soul at the meeting; the step the 'in this life' argument needs as its contrast.

¶20.label: advance
¶20.why: Every soul takes part because every soul can perceive God, and the soul sees itself as it is. The three-item roadmap is scaffolding, but the claim is new.

¶21.label: advance
¶21.why: What is seen at the meeting is the soul as a reflection of God: the 'reflected in the soul' step of this section's point. The mercy/justice sentence is a side detail.

¶22.label: aside
¶22.why: That the soul cannot encompass God is a limit the point does not need; only ¶20's roadmap makes it seem owed. Deleting it (and trimming the roadmap) breaks nothing. Khomeini is a second authority for the same limit.

¶23.label: advance
¶23.why: What is perceived then depends on what is perceived now: the step that makes 'in this life' follow.

¶24.label: advance
¶24.why: States the 'in this life' conclusion and adds the second reason (death's journey is harder). Its last sentence repeats ¶18.

¶25.label: aside
¶25.why: A third scholar describing the unveiled self and tying it to the hadith. ¶26 is already supported by ¶18 (purifying) and ¶21 (what is seen is the soul); nothing later uses Maliki Tabrizi.

¶26.label: restate
¶26.why: Summarises ¶17, ¶18 and ¶21. 'The way to God runs through knowing and purifying the self' adds no new link; the conclusion has been reached by ¶24.

¶27.label: aside
¶27.why: A bridge question for the next chapter, not a step toward this section's point; the chapter raises it and does not answer it.
